issues.legal_issue: A bequest of a specified quantity from a larger identified property is not void for uncertainty when the testator’s intention is clear and the uncertainty can be resolved by selection; absent a selection by the testator or a person appointed by the testator, the legatee may select.
material_facts: The will specified the quantity and kinds of land to be given to the beneficiaries from an identified larger area, but did not identify the particular parcels.
The area of each kind of land in the identified property exceeded the quantity bequeathed.
The testator neither selected the parcels nor appointed another person to make the selection.
issues.conclusion: The bequest was not void for uncertainty under section 89 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925. The beneficiaries were entitled to select the land bequeathed to them.
issues.legal_principle: Section 89 applies where the will is so indefinite that no definite intention can be ascertained; it does not invalidate a gift whose clear intention can be made certain by selection. The benevolent rule permitting selection by the legatee is a common-sense rule applicable in India in appropriate cases. The Court approved Narayanasami Gramani v. Periathambi Gramani (1895) I.L.R. 18 Mad. 460, discussed Bharadwaja Mudaliar v. Kolandavelu Mudaliar (1915) 29 M.L.J. 717, and referred to Hobson v. Blackburn, Peck v. Halsey, Tapley v. Eagleton, Duckmanton v. Duckmanton, and Knapton v. Hindle. Asten v. Asten and Bishop v. Holt were distinguished as inapplicable.

rule.if: will_bequest_civil_appeal and specified_quantity_from_identified_larger_property and testator_intention_clear and uncertainty_resolvable_by_selection and not testator_selected_property and not selection_agent_appointed

predicates.will_bequest_civil_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal concerning the construction of a bequest in a will.
predicates.specified_quantity_from_identified_large: The testator specified a quantity of property to be taken from a larger identified property.
predicates.testator_intention_clear: The words of the will show a definite intention to make the gift, even though they do not identify the particular property to be taken.
predicates.uncertainty_resolvable_by_selection: A selection from the identified property can make the subject of the gift definite.
predicates.testator_selected_property: The testator identified the particular property to be given to the legatee.
predicates.selection_agent_appointed: The testator appointed another person to select the property for the legatee.
predicates.legatee_may_select_and_bequest_is_valid: The legatee may select the property and the bequest is not void for uncertainty.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a clear bequest of a specified quantity from larger identified property, and selection can resolve the uncertainty, the legatee may select if neither the testator nor an appointed agent selected the property, and the bequest remains valid.

issues.legal_issue: A direction that a guardian deliver specified land to beneficiaries when they attain majority does not, without words appointing the guardian to select the land, give the guardian the selection right.
material_facts: The will appointed the testator’s brother as guardian of the minor beneficiaries and placed the property under his management.
The will directed the guardian to give each beneficiary a specified quantity of two kinds of land from an identified area when the beneficiaries attained majority.
The will separately directed the guardian to deliver the remaining properties to another beneficiary upon that beneficiary attaining majority.
The will contained no words appointing the guardian to choose the parcels or requiring the land to be divided by quality.
issues.conclusion: The guardian was not given the right to select the land. The beneficiaries had the right to select their respective land from the identified area.
issues.legal_principle: The will must be construed to determine whether the testator selected the property or appointed a third person to do so. A direction to deliver property, read in context as a direction to transfer possession when beneficiaries attain majority, does not itself appoint the guardian as selector. Where the testator has not selected the property or appointed a selector, and the intended gift can be made definite by selection, the rule stated in Narayanasami Gramani v. Periathambi Gramani (1895) I.L.R. 18 Mad. 460 applies; the Court also treated the observations in Bharadwaja Mudaliar v. Kolandavelu Mudaliar (1915) 29 M.L.J. 717 about court partition as unnecessary to that case.

predicates.civil_appeal_concerning_will_constructio: The proceeding is a civil appeal concerning the construction of a will.
predicates.guardian_directed_to_deliver_specified_p: The testator directed a guardian to deliver specified property to beneficiaries when they attained majority.
predicates.will_does_not_appoint_guardian_to_select: The will contains no words appointing the guardian to choose the property to be given.
predicates.gift_can_be_made_definite_by_beneficiary: The intended gift can be made definite by the beneficiaries choosing property from the identified larger area.
predicates.beneficiaries_have_selection_right: The beneficiaries are entitled to select the property bequeathed to them.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns a will directing a guardian to deliver specified property at majority, the beneficiaries have the selection right if the will does not appoint the guardian to select and their selection can make the gift definite.
